steps.en: What you see: The right ventricular outflow tract funnels upward into the thin pulmonary cusps and the pulmonary trunk. The aortic root sits behind, cut in short axis, as a reminder of how anterior this plane is.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Pressure drop in mmHg equals 4 times the peak velocity in m per s squared.
Tricuspid regurgitation peak velocity 2.8 m per s or less is normal.
Report outflow acceleration time with the heart rate, since it shortens as pulmonary pressure rises.

Pitfalls: The pulmonary valve is thin and fast, so freeze in systole with a high frame rate before calling stenosis. trivial pulmonary regurgitation is common and normal; only a dense wide jet with a steep slope matters.

Left anterior cusp of pulmonary valve

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Cutting through the aortic root instead of the pulmonary valve. Correct it by rotating further anticlockwise until the round aorta gives way to the tubular pulmonary trunk.
Losing the pulmonary trunk bifurcation by rotating too far. Correct it by rotating back clockwise a touch until the trunk lengthens without dividing.
Rib shadow wiping out the valve in systole. Correct it by sliding one space down and asking for a held breath out.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, second or third intercostal space, rotated anticlockwise from long axis.
Point the probe marker toward the left shoulder, about one o clock.
Rotate anticlockwise from the long axis in the second or third space until the aorta disappears and the pulmonary trunk lengthens. If the aorta stays on screen, keep rotating.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Set colour across the pulmonary valve for regurgitation and stenosis.

q.en: Which rotation from the long axis opens the outflow view?

why.en: Anticlockwise rotation in the second or third space opens the pulmonary valve.

q.en: Pulmonary velocity is 1 m per s. What is the peak pressure drop?

why.en: Four times one squared is 4 mmHg, a normal low gradient.

q.en: A thin diastolic jet fills one third of the outflow. What is this?

why.en: A thin jet is trivial and common; density and width decide severity.

q.en: Rib shadow wipes out the valve in systole. What helps?

o.en: Slide one space down with held breath out

why.en: A lower space with held breath out moves lung and rib off the valve.
